prerequisites: ELASTICITY AND STRENGTH OF MATERIALS I/20224106
ELASTICITY AND STRENGTH OF MATERIALS II/20224107

learning_outcomes.text: Calculates and designs structures and industrial constructions. Applies graphic engineering techniques.
Carries out preliminary industrial construction projects.
Capacity for designing structures according to standardized criteria. Knows the urban planning conditions that affect industrial implementation.
Prepares technical reports. Applies topographical techniques to field problems.
Uses methodologies for preparing and formulating reports and projects. Carries out preliminary projects within their specialty.
Uses structural calculation and finite element software.
Generates the plans and appropriate documentation for industrial construction.
Knows and applies methods for calculating structures. Capacity for the conception and development of an Industrial Plant Project.

syllabus_topics: Urban planning conditions. Urban planning utilization.
The industrial plant project, implementation criteria.
Building elements of the industrial building. The Technical Building Code.
Exterior enclosures of industrial buildings, facades.
Exterior enclosures of industrial buildings, roofs.
teaching_methods: Introductory activities: Video and PowerPoint presentations of works, building projects, etc.
Lecture session: Presentation and theoretical explanation of the subject's program.
Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom: Delivery of exercises and practices, formulation, resolution and debate of problems related to the subject's topic.
Personalized attention: There will be personalized attention hours.

assessment_methods.method: Problem/exercise solving in the ordinary classroom (practices)

assessment_rules: For continuous assessment, students with a total qualification above 75% from practices and partial exams may pass without attending the first call, provided all individual grades are above 4.5. Submissions via Moodle must be uploaded within the marked timeframe; late submissions receive a ZERO. In the first call, a minimum score of 4 out of 10 in the final exam is required to average with other assessment notes; otherwise, the first call grade will be solely the final exam grade. For the second call, only an exam consisting of short questions and practical tests will be evaluated, and no grades obtained during the course will be considered, though favorable aspects from the first call may be taken into consideration. Fraudulent performance of any evaluative activity, including the use of AI, will result in a failing grade for that activity and may lead to disciplinary action.
